subject: Default capture scope — session fragments vs final outputs
messages:
From: Shira Goldberg <shira@clearwelllabs.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Aaron Chu <aaron.chu@clearwelllabs.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: what Redwood keeps by default (stream fragments vs final completions)

Hi Vanessa,

We’re finalizing our security questionnaire for Clearwell’s pilot and a couple of things around default capture are still fuzzy for my legal/procurement team. We want a short, definitive answer we can put into the MSA. Specifics below — can you confirm?

1) For interactive sessions (webchat / streaming token responses) — do you persist partial fragments (intermediate streamed tokens) by default, or only the finalized completion? If fragments are kept, what is the retention window?

2) How do you classify “prompt” vs “generated output”? Is the user-supplied input treated differently for retention than model outputs?

3) Where do defaults differ between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments?

4) What’s the deletion/erasure process if we request account-wide purge and what evidence do you provide?

I attached our questionnaire page and the sections we need to populate. If you can provide a one-paragraph answer we can circulate internally that would be great.

Thanks,
Shira Goldberg
Head of Security Operations
Clearwell Labs
shira@clearwelllabs.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com

Cc: Aaron Chu <aaron.chu@clearwelllabs.com>, kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q: what Redwood keeps by default (stream fragments vs final completions)

Hi Shira — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ve looped in Kimberly (policy) to confirm specifics and provide exact wording you can drop into the MSA.

- Short answers: by default we persist request metadata and the full request payload (the prompt) for 30 days; model-generated final completions are retained for 90 days for tooling/telemetry by default. Streaming fragments (intermediate token buffers) are not written to long-term storage by default — they are held in ephemeral buffers and are eligible for short-term telemetry that is typically purged within 24 hours, unless the session finalizes and the final completion gets recorded per the 90-day rule.

- Prompts vs outputs: prompts (user-supplied text) and model outputs are distinct artifacts in our system and treated separately for retention and redaction. Prompts are treated as request data; outputs are treated as generated artifacts.

- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: Hosted follows the default above. Dedicated (reserved capacity) allows contractable retention windows and additional options (longer or shorter) under a reserved-capacity SOW. Private (VPC/on-prem) means your team controls storage and the default retention is governed by your deployment config — Redwood does not persist customer data in the control plane for on-prem setups by default.

I’ll let Kimberly paste a concise paragraph for legal and include the erase evidence steps.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Quick Q: what Redwood keeps by default (stream fragments vs final completions)

Hi Shira — Kimberly from Policy here. Below is a one‑paragraph statement you can paste into your MSA plus a short Q&A for the bits you called out.

MSA language (suggested): "By default, Redwood Inference retains request payloads (prompts and metadata) for 30 calendar days and generated final outputs for 90 calendar days for operational telemetry and quality monitoring. Ephemeral streaming fragments (intermediate token buffers emitted during a streaming response) are not written to persistent storage by default and are purged from ephemeral buffers within 24 hours unless a session explicitly finalizes and the final output is captured. Retention behavior can be adjusted for Dedicated or Private deployments by mutual agreement and is subject to the applicable SOW."

Clarifying Q&A:
- Streaming fragments: ephemeral by default; not persisted to long-term storage. Short-term telemetry traces that include fragment-level timing may be retained up to 24 hours and are automatically purged.
- Prompts: the full prompt text is retained as request data for 30 days by default; customers can opt into shorter windows in Hosted via API flags or request a custom retention for Dedicated.
- Outputs: final completions are retained 90 days by default to support regressions, QA, and billing reconciliation; customers can request deletion at any time via a support ticket.
- Deletion/erasure evidence: for Hosted customers we provide a deletion job ID and timestamp plus a short report (CSV) of affected record IDs. For Dedicated/Private customers deletion protocols are implemented per the SOW and Redwood will coordinate with the customer to provide equivalent evidence.
- EU/residency: retention windows above are tenant defaults; data residency (where data is stored) can be constrained to EU regions for EU customers — retention periods remain configurable by contract.

Next steps: if Clearwell needs the MSA clause to specify a different default window please indicate the desired windows (prompts / outputs / telemetry) and we will generate a redline.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Policy
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood-inference.com
